headline: Orlando's fan year follows the tourist calendar, and the playoffs set the peak.
summary: Orlando's fan year is playoff-gated: it spikes in April and May and sags in the summer heat. Sales follow the tourism calendar as much as the standings. With no opening-night or Christmas Day game, the first real spike is the Cup Friday run in Nov. New coach Sean Sweeney inherits a young core, with Vucevic back at center.

insights.title: Playoff-gated peak, summer trough
insights.detail: Engagement peaks in April-May, when the Magic are in the postseason, and bottoms out in July-September. The only team news then is the Orlando Summer League and draft aftermath, in peak heat and hurricane season. Last season's 45-37 team got in as the 8 seed, beat Charlotte in the Play-In and went out to Detroit in the first round, so the spring peak was short.
insights.implication: Hold the biggest apparel drop for a playoff-ready window (mid-March to April). Keep summer product to lifestyle and heritage, not performance jerseys.

insights.title: The visitor multiplier
insights.detail: Orlando's tourism economy fills Kia Center in Dec, Mar and the summer school breaks with out-of-market buyers. They treat the Magic as a souvenir, not a loyalty badge. Visitors buy in the arena and at Disney Springs-area retail rather than online.
insights.implication: Build a small giftable, travel-friendly capsule (tees, caps, packable items) priced for visitors. Keep it separate from the locals' jersey-and-City-Edition stack.

insights.title: Black Friday to Christmas is a Cup winter
insights.detail: The Magic are in Emirates NBA Cup East Group A with Detroit, Toronto, Milwaukee and Brooklyn. Group games fall on Fridays from Oct 30 to Nov 27. With no opening-night or Christmas Day game, holiday hoops attention goes elsewhere.
insights.implication: Make Cup Friday nights the local event and the Cup colorway or tee the gift item. Don't lean on national-TV moments the Magic don't have.

insights.title: Football and Florida fall compete directly
insights.detail: From September to December, UCF Knights, Florida, Florida State and Miami football dominate local sports attention. So does the Florida Classic in Orlando in November. Orlando City SC and the Orlando Pride share the same fall calendar.
insights.implication: Don't launch performance basketball product in October. Use collegiate-adjacent crossover looks, and let the Magic's pinstripe heritage stand apart from football.

insights.title: Heritage nostalgia is a second engine
insights.detail: The 1995 Finals team (Shaquille O'Neal, Penny Hardaway, Nick Anderson) and the 2009 Dwight Howard Finals team anchor local identity for fans who grew up in the 90s. So do the pinstripe jerseys. The feeling peaks around the draft, 'Throwback' nights and opening weeks.
insights.implication: Pair every Banchero-era release with a Penny-era pinstripe or star-motif story. Older and younger fans each get a reason to buy.

insights.title: Hurricane season sets a quiet clock
insights.detail: Atlantic hurricane season runs June to November. A storm week can cancel local events and shift game schedules or shipping. Peak risk is Aug-Oct, just when preseason hype and early retail would normally build.
insights.implication: Plan a flexible ship window for the Oct-Nov drops. Don't tie a one-night event to a single early-season date.

The team, plus the city's 'Magic Kingdom' halo, which locals joke about and avoid overusing.
Orlando's long-standing area code, used as local pride shorthand.
Locals' term for peak visitor months, when traffic and prices rise.

designCues.use: Use as the base for Association and gift items, so the read is instantly Orlando.

designCues.source: Franchise secondary silver and the 90s palette
designCues.use: Metallic trim or reflective detail on throwback-inspired pieces.
Statement and night-game pieces. Pairs with blue for the modern look.

designCues.source: The 1990s Magic pinstripe uniforms and star motif
designCues.use: Apply to a heritage capsule with clear credit to the Penny-era design. Check licensing for any retired marks.
Lightweight, quick-dry knits and mesh for tees and warm-ups that work through the long summer.

designCues.cue: Sunset gradient from lake and sky
designCues.source: Central Florida evening skies over downtown lakes
designCues.use: A subtle fade on gift tees and caps, not a direct theme-park reference.

productHooks: A March-April playoff-push capsule (tee, warm-up, cap) timed to the Play-In window, plus a quick-turn plan for rally towels and playoff tees.
A heritage pinstripe capsule built around the 90s Magic, released for the Cup Friday run and holiday gifting.
A visitor gift line sold at Kia Center and tourist retail: packable tees and caps in Magic blue, priced as souvenirs.
A lightweight summer line timed to Orlando Summer League and school break, for fans who engage only at the margins.
watchouts: Avoid Disney, Universal and theme-park character or logo cues. They are heavily licensed third-party IP.
Pulse remembrance and the LGBTQ+ and Latino communities connected to it are not marketing hooks.
Don't hinge a plan on a healthy-Wagner spring. Offer product that works if the team stumbles.
Some schedule details are not yet verified. Confirm home dates before locking events.

keyDates.name: NBA season opens (no Magic game)
keyDates.why: A tripleheader on NBC without the Magic, so their own opener needs separate planning.

keyDates.name: NBA Cup group play starts
keyDates.why: The Magic play East Group A with Detroit, Toronto, Milwaukee and Brooklyn on Fridays through Nov 27.

keyDates.name: NBA Cup knockouts and final
keyDates.why: Semifinals at the higher seeds' home arenas. The final is at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis on Dec 11.
